summary: Frontend E2E test of the new ORA Guide mascot system (replaces GlobalHelpFAB). Signed up a fresh user via API, injected token, and validated all 12 feature scenarios in the review request. All critical flows pass: mascot hidden on /login,/,/admin-guarded routes; single fixed-position element (old GlobalHelpFAB no longer mounted); stage4 auto-bubble fires with correct copy + orange spotlight class applied to data-guide-target=connect-github-btn; sessionStorage dedup key ora_guide_seen_v1_connect_github is set to '1' and prevents re-open across reload; general help panel (Open Advisor / Contact support / Close) renders on manual click; Open Advisor dispatches `aurem:ora-open` window event exactly once and closes the bubble; Contact support creates a real ticket in cto_support with source='in_app_guide', subject 'ORA Guide — stuck at: general', body includes stage/page/ISO timestamp, viewable in admin support panel, then auto-closes. First-message chips correctly absent when no project exists.
critical_code_review_comments: OraGuideMascot.jsx `useEffect` cleanup: `pollRef.current` is captured at cleanup time — safe now, but if `hidden` toggles mid-lifecycle the previous interval could leak. Consider capturing `intervalId` locally inside effect and clearing that.

In OraGuideMascot.setTimeout(1400) after escalated confirm, if user navigates or clicks avatar in that window, panelMode gets reset to 'stage' even in general mode — cosmetic only. Consider guarding with `if (!open) return;` inside timeout.

sessionStorage.setItem is fire-once but stage-change auto-close (line 100-104) does not clear the seen key. If a user finishes step1 (auto-closes bubble for connect_github) then somehow regresses (unusual but possible via GH uninstall) the bubble won't reopen this session. Acceptable per 'once per session' spec but worth calling out.

GlobalHelpFAB.jsx is kept mounted-less but still imported for `shouldHide`/`HIDE_PREFIXES`. Good — but consider extracting those constants to a tiny helpers module to make the intent obvious (GlobalHelpFAB looks like a dead component otherwise).

Chip disappearance is driven by `messages.length <= 1` (synthetic WELCOME=1). If a project has 0 messages (e.g., WELCOME failed to seed), the condition still holds (`<=1`) so chips still show — safe. If in future WELCOME becomes 2 messages the condition breaks silently — consider an explicit flag.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (12/12 scenarios pass, chip-visible + stage2/3 auto-open validated by main-agent screenshots already)
